The Manager, Development Applications Section, Department Of Arts, Heritage And The Gaeltacht Newtown Road Wexford Date:    2 October, 2015             Register Ref:   F15A/0183            Development: The construction of 190 houses and 60 apartments.  The proposed houses comprise 72 no. four bedroom two storey houses, 15 no. three bedroom three storey houses and 103 no. three bedroom two storey houses.  The proposed apartments are within four blocks of 15 apartments each comprising 4 no. one bedroom apartments and 11 no. two bedroom apartments in three storey plus penthouse.  The development includes all associated site works and infrastructure which includes landscaped open space, internal roads, paths, cycle-paths, public lighting, utilities, drainage and surface water attenuation.  This application is accompanied by an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS), which will be available for inspection or purchase for a fee not exceeding the reasonable costs of making a copy at the offices of Fingal County Council during its public opening hours.            Location: Lands South of the Rathbeale Road, Mooretown, Swords, Co. Dublin.            Applicant:   Gannon Properties            App. Type:   Permission            Date  Recd :   10 August, 2015 Dear Sir/Madam, With reference to the above,  CLARIFICATION OF ADDITIONAL INFORMATION  was requested from the Agent/Applicant in relation to this application on  1 October, 2015 .  Details of this Clarification of Additional Information are attached for your information. You will be notified when a response to the request for Clarification of Additional Information is received by the Planning Authority.        Yours faithfully, __________________________ for   Senior Executive Officer Details of Clarification of Additional Information sought LOCATION: Lands South of the Rathbeale Road, Mooretown, Swords, Co. Dublin. The response to Item No. 8 of the request for Additional Information dated 17th June 2015 is unsatisfactory and does not address the serious outstanding issues with respect to the provision of public open space required to serve this large residential development. In this regard, the Applicant is required to address the following: (a)  The Applicant is requested to provide Clarification of Additional Information with respect to the manner in which Class 1 open space to serve this development is to be provided and delivered.  In this regard, the attention of the Applicant is directed to the requirements of Section 3.1.5 of the Oldtown Mooretown Local Area Plan and the Phasing arrangements as set out under Section 4 Phasing and Implementation.  The LAP clearly indicates that active Class 1 public open space shall be located within the Swords Regional Park and such areas shall be provided and developed at the Developer’s expense, dedicated as public open space and kept free of development in accordance with the phasing strategy for such lands.   The Applicant is requested to provide Clarification of Additional Information in the relation to the manner in which it is proposed comply with the requirements of the LAP in this regard. (b)  The Applicant is requested to provide Clarification of Additional Information with regard to the significant extent of surface water attenuation/SUDs features which are proposed on areas of Class 2 public open space.  Section 3.1.5 of the Oldtown Mooretown LAP states that SuDs areas will not form part of the calculations for Class 2 public open space provision within the lands except where they contribute in a significant way to design and quality of open space.  Revised drawings submitted by Waterman Moylan Consulting Engineers submitted by way of Additional Information indicate extensive areas of SuDs in the Watermill Park area which significantly limits the ability of these lands to function appropriately as areas of open space. The response to Item No. 5 is unsatisfactory and does not address the shortfall in private open space required to serve these apartment units.  The Applicant is requested to submit by way of Clarification of Additional Information, revised plans detailing an increase in the area of the balconies in question such that they comply in full with the requirements of Objectives OS40 and OS41 of the Development Plan. The Additional Information response details a site for childcare facility on the southern corner junction of Road 9 and Road 8.  No building has been proposed or layout provided. Having regard to the scale of the residential development proposed, it is not considered that the allocation of a single site would be sufficient in terms of meeting the requirements of the Childcare Guidelines 2001 and would not comply in general with the requirement to provide new communities/larger housing schemes which require at least one childcare facility for 75 dwellings.  Given the timeframe for the delivery of serviced centres within the overall land holding it is imperative that appropriately located childcare facilities to meet expected demand are provided at appropriate locations within this residential scheme. Accordingly, the Applicant is requested to submit Clarification of Additional Information with regard to the manner in which the development complies with childcare requirements.

development at Drumnigh near Portmarnock, Co. Dublin.Following an additional
information(Al) request from FCC, AWN Consulting Ltd was subsequently retained
by McCrossan O'Rourke Manning Architects to undertake an inward noise impact
assessment. Additionally, the Al also requested that construction noise impacts
associated with theproposed development be assessed.
The site in question, currently greenfield lands,is bound to the north by residential
dwellings and to the south by greenfield lands. The R124 Drumnigh Road bounds the
site to the west whilst theMalahide DART lineruns along the site to the east.
Thesite islocated approximately 5km east of Dublin Airport.Figure 2 illustrates the
site'location in the context of the Airport.The location of the site and dwellings are
within the outer airport noise zone as designated by the Fingal County Council
DevelopmentPlan2011-2017.
The proposed development will comprise of 270 no. two storey residential dwellings.
The proposed dwellings are a combination of 3, 4 and 5 bedroom designs.
To address the relevant noise concerns, the following has been included as part of
this report:

assessment;

sensitivelocations,and;

noise incident on the site.

The site of the proposed development was examined in daylight and overnight on September

use of three different bat detectors with the capacity to convert bat signals to an audible
format (heterodyne and time expansion) and recordable formats (time expansion and
frequency division). This allows for an identification of bats in the field and subsequently
from recordings made on a SD card upon a computer sound analysis program.
One bat detector (SD2) was left in line with the internal hedge that serves as the main focus
of this assessment for a period of two hours from 7.30 pm to record any evidence of emerging
or commuting bats. This detector was then installed in a Portacabin to continue monitoring up
todawn out of view andout of anypotential inclementweather.
A second bat detector, a Pettersson D240X time expansion and heterodyne detector was held
and used for analysis of all other bat activity while traversing the site and surrounding roads
and hedgerow. This detector has a highly sensitive transducer for recording bat signals both
in converted form (heterodyne) as well as producing a signal 1/10 the speed of the original
signal (time expanded) and thus audible to the human ear.A third detector was also hand-
held (EM3) and carried during survey of the site. This allowed for instant identification of
any bats encountered during this aspect of the survey.

Potential Impacts of development
Loss of feeding
Construction leads to the removal of some trees and other scrubvegetation and there is often
a consequent loss in insect abundance and resting and breeding sites. This has a knock-on
effect on insectivores such as bats and birds. This is likely to be to a slight to moderate
permanent negativeimpactfrom thisproject.
There will be a loss of scrub and some tree removal on the perimeter of the site. The
remainder of the site is an open field and there will be loss of grassland but no substantial
plants.
There will be an increase in concrete areas and a control on garden plants with pesticide. This
may further reduce insect abundance.However, as this area is often planted with cereal (and
is likely to undergo rotation to pasture and back), there is likely to be high residues within the
soil of various pesticides. This would reduce in times of pasture but would again increase
when cereals are grown.
6
Mitigation Measures
Restriction on illumination to protect bat roosts and feeding areas
Ornamental Lighting should be avoided as this inhibits bat roosting or delays emergence
(should bats occupy the building) and interrupts feeding success of some bat species and
potentially breeding success. There are no existing roosts likely to be affected in the
immediate area of theproposal.
Planting
As vegetation will be removed to facilitate construction, it should be replaced and wherever
possible enhanced. When planting is considered, native and local plant species should be
empioyed including typical plants such as hawthorn, blackthorn, elder, gorse, bramble, in
addition to other species such as dog rose and Clematis attractive to moths.
Plants such as Lonicera periclymenum (honeysuckle) are beneficial to moths and other
nocturnal insects while Hebe and Buddleja are beneficial to daytime and some night insects.
Bees would benefit from lavender, jasmine, rosemary, violets, thyme, blue bells, wisteria,
cone flowers and sunflowers.
The area of most significance is the hedge on the western edge of the site. This section should
be re-plantedwith mature trees and understorey.
Residual Impacts from theDevelopment
There will be a decrease in vegetation and a consequent reduction in feeding on site. There
will be a loss of roost potential from removal of mature trees. These will both be
compensated by bat box provision and planting. Following this, there will be a slight negative
impact.
